admitted.text: Randi reads as a woman whose beauty is armor she rebuilt in a mirror the same night a man saw past it
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Randi reads as genuinely and helplessly drawn to Vee from the start, not merely performing desire for Pace's benefit.
admitted.detail_quote: The word came out alone, with nothing around it — the bare arrival of a thing already true before she got to it.

admitted.text: She seems to draw Vee's secrets out on purpose and then cut her off at the peak, which reads as control dressed up as kindness.
admitted.detail_quote: It was gentle. It was kind. It was a door closing softly.

admitted.text: Randi seems to use small hidden hurts to regulate emotional pressure she cannot acknowledge openly.
admitted.detail_quote: She had the rim of her glass in under her thumbnail, pressing, and she held it there until she set the glass down.

admitted.text: In rare unguarded moments she lets herself be fed, which reads as a hunger she usually denies coming briefly through.
admitted.detail_quote: and used the fork to gather what was left at the edge of the plate.

admitted.text: Her feelings for Vee seem to have grown beyond the game into a real attachment she doesn't fully understand.
admitted.detail_quote: I keep waiting to get bored of her — I get bored of everybody — and it doesn't come.

admitted.text: Her resentment of Pace's pace with Vee, and of his weekends with her, seems to be cracking the couple's easy closeness.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi went still on him. Not the loose stillness of after. A different one, the kind that takes holding.

admitted.text: Randi seems capable of violating both lovers while experiencing the violation as tenderness and play.
admitted.detail_quote: She touched the picture and sent it to herself.

admitted.text: Randi reads as tender despite all her management, moved by Vee's gladness to something real in Kentucky
admitted.detail_quote: She laughed. It came out of her without a sound, and she put her hand over her mouth, and her eyes stung.

admitted.text: Randi reads as a practiced social strategist, able to manufacture an apparently accidental intimacy with exquisite precision.
admitted.detail_quote: We should have been sitting in the first row as she took a long step, showing those legs all the way to the hip, tits out.

admitted.text: Randi reads as possessive of firsts — what she wants from Vee is to be the one remembered at eighty
admitted.detail_quote: She'll be eighty years old and she'll remember the first one.

admitted.text: His care reads as precise and close attention, as if noticing were his way of loving.
admitted.detail_quote: he had laid the slices in the bowl with the cut sides up because he had noticed that she ate them faster when the cut sides showed

admitted.text: He seems truly devoted to consent, and holds to it even when Randi pushes him to hurry.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: All the same, he seems comfortable keeping Vee in the dark about the plan she was chosen for, and even enjoys it.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: His appetite seems partly to be the watcher's pleasure of setting up what other people will feel.
admitted.detail_quote: He was building in her the kind of need that could not be denied.

admitted.text: For all his perceptiveness with Vee, he seems oddly blind to what Randi is going through.
admitted.detail_quote: Somehow Randi had gone right past all of it, and every conversation since the airport had gone just where she wanted it.

admitted.text: Pace reads as guarding Vee's private gifts even from the woman he shares the plan with
admitted.detail_quote: That she had given him herself, in the truck with the rain coming down, and he kept it.

admitted.text: He seems to defend his teenage relationship with Daphne as luck, without seeing the harm in it.
admitted.detail_quote: That he had handed her the thing that had hurt him and named it luck.

admitted.text: His respect for closed doors reads as a lesson learned from a past wound.
admitted.detail_quote: A closed door was hers, not his; you did not open it just because you could hear through it.

admitted.text: Pace reads as twenty-two and carrying a scar and a "not tonight" the book has not opened
admitted.detail_quote: It came out of him harder than anything he had ever said to her.

admitted.text: Pace reads as a prodigy who learned his gentleness late, as a repair of early harm he still describes without self-pity
admitted.detail_quote: So she moved my desk into the hall during math class, and I did long-division worksheets.

admitted.text: Vee reads as quietly starving — for food, for being seen, for a life with color in it
admitted.detail_quote: It kept going down and down into something that had been empty a lot longer than since noon.

admitted.text: She seems hungry to belong, and dazzled at being chosen by someone like Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: that she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand, by exactly the person she'd have chosen to be chosen by.

admitted.text: Vee reads as wired so shame and wanting run on the same wire, and she has stopped looking for a seam
admitted.detail_quote: she could not find the seam between the heat and the shame because there was no seam, they ran on the same wire

admitted.text: Her attraction to Randi seems real but unadmitted, something she has no place for in her picture of herself.
admitted.detail_quote: the heat the picture put low in Vee was a heat she had no shelf for and would have died before naming at this table.

admitted.text: Vee reads as dangerously trusting because she mistakes the apparent chance of meeting Randi and Pace for extraordinary good fortune.
admitted.detail_quote: She had never been so fortunate, or so happy.

admitted.text: She seems to be drifting from Cassie, quietly editing her life for her oldest friend.
admitted.detail_quote: She lifted it out clean as she went, the way a ladle takes soup from the pot and the surface closes without a hole

admitted.text: Vee reads as newly powerful, spending a body she only just found out she had
admitted.detail_quote: that she had nearly toppled this contained, careful man — *her*, she'd nearly done that — and that he'd stayed on his knees finishing her hem anyway

admitted.text: Her new boldness reads as chosen, a deliberate act of display.
admitted.detail_quote: He was already walking away and I pulled him back and I did it. Me.

admitted.text: She seems to be overreaching with money to keep up with Randi's world, at a real cost to herself.
admitted.detail_quote: that she did not have the next part, the paying-it-back part, that it would be sitting there next month

admitted.text: She seems to sense something wrong about Randi from the very start.
admitted.detail_quote: something passed over her face, brief, that Vee would not have been able to name

admitted.text: She reads as quietly protective, with loyalty that asks for nothing back.
admitted.detail_quote: How much did he give you to drink?

admitted.text: She seems hurt at being pushed aside, and hides it.
admitted.detail_quote: the whole word, flat and finished, the word for a longer parting than a Wednesday.

admitted.text: She seems to be the one who cares about Vee herself rather than about the glamour around her.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend

admitted.text: She reads as a watchful authority with more power than Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: Her warmth reads as a measuring look, something like an appraisal.
admitted.detail_quote: felt it take her measure, top to bottom, and stay warm the whole way.

admitted.text: Sloane reads as the sorority house's ambient weather, laughing at whatever comes and meaning none of it
admitted.detail_quote: Sloane laughed her laugh, the laugh that meant nothing on its own and was therefore available for anything.

admitted.text: Kinsey reads as the house's echo, matching pitches she has had no time to choose
admitted.detail_quote: The matching was very fast. She had not had time to choose the pitch.

admitted.text: Meg reads as steady and knowing, the friend with the long view of boys and no need to press it
admitted.detail_quote: Everybody's different at the start. I said it about Danny. Word for word, I think.

admitted.text: Kayla reads as the bright chorus who names out loud what Vee will not let herself know
admitted.detail_quote: We're doing hair Saturday. I'm coming to your room. This is happening.

admitted.text: Christine reads as proof of Pace's long quiet debts of affection, paid in return visits
admitted.detail_quote: Christine fed me twice what I ordered and wouldn't put it on the bill. I've been coming back to get even.

admitted.text: Theo reads as the nice boy Vee measures against a man, and the measuring is not close
admitted.detail_quote: He took it like a gentleman. He's nice.

admitted.text: She seems to have been the tender center of Pace's lonely adolescence, which is also the troubling part.
admitted.detail_quote: She was twenty-one and I was seventeen, and the rooms she was walking into by then were rooms they wouldn't let me stand in for four more years.

admitted.text: She reads as the source of the shaming voice that Vee carries in her head.
admitted.detail_quote: the word arriving whole and in her mother's voice before she had finished forming the picture

admitted.text: The bench hidden under a table top: the desire under the house's polite surface, always waiting to be uncovered again.
admitted.detail_quote: it would sit there in the middle of the room, full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The deadbolt and the lock: Randi sealing herself away even inside her intimacy with Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: the small click of the lock turning over, which was not a thing she had ever done before in his house.

admitted.text: Thin-sliced apples: Randi's rationed appetite, and Pace's wish to feed her.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: Euler's cross, two hard things made simple by putting them together at right angles: it reads as a figure for the planned threesome.
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: The burgundy dress: reads as Pace’s attention made wearable and as the bolder self Vee learns to inhabit.
admitted.detail_quote: Everything she'd ever worn had been cut for no one in particular. This one had been cut to the actual shape of her, and to no one else's.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt, whose smell is fading: Vee's longing for the real man behind what stands in for him.
admitted.detail_quote: That night she lay in the flannel in the dark, her nose to the collar, and breathed him in

admitted.text: The folded green panties given as a "trade": Vee's shame turned into a gift she offers.
admitted.detail_quote: the deep green of them particular and chosen, and the spot exactly where she'd put it.

admitted.text: Leave no trace: Pace's ethic of taking nothing and leaving nothing, which later echoes darkly.
admitted.detail_quote: We take nothing and leave nothing," he said.

admitted.text: The cherry pits on wax paper: reads as instruction without humiliation, a tiny model of the care Vee is starving for.
admitted.detail_quote: She had it now. She had it and he hadn't made her small to give it to her.

admitted.text: Randi deleting messages from Pace's phone: "leave no trace" turned into covering up a deception.
admitted.detail_quote: the magnet took it with the same small click, and the screen lit and went dark again.

admitted.text: Error-correcting codes: meaning that survives noise through repetition, the way the novel's repeated gestures do.
admitted.detail_quote: Say it more than once so the noise can't kill it.

admitted.text: The pool: the one place where Vee's body was never a problem for her.
admitted.detail_quote: Nobody up there could see her. Nobody down here wanted anything.

admitted.text: Randi's untouched bowl, put away "for her": care that is offered and refused, and kept anyway.
admitted.detail_quote: Her bowl on the table where he had set it down, the sauce gone to a skin over the peas and the carrot

admitted.text: The two towels: read as an already-prepared place for another person inside Pace’s orderly solitary life.
admitted.detail_quote: Down a hall to the left: a bathroom, plain, clean, two towels on the rod.

admitted.text: The black heels: read as borrowed social confidence purchased beyond Vee’s means, beautiful support carrying a hidden debt.
admitted.detail_quote: standing in them felt less like wearing a shoe than being stood up by one.

admitted.text: The cardigan buttoned to the throat: reads as the mother's verdict made fabric, the apology Vee wears over the better shirt
admitted.detail_quote: She kept her cardigan where it was. She had worn the cardigan over the better shirt on purpose this morning

admitted.text: The high table in the window: reads as Vee's hunger to be displayed and her dread of it, set on a shelf and glad
admitted.detail_quote: up in the window, feet off the floor, her body presented at the height the whole room could see

admitted.text: The long second step on stage: reads as the secret under the silk becoming a public act only she can read
admitted.detail_quote: and the room knew, and not a soul in it could have said so out loud.

admitted.text: What caused the large scar high on Pace’s thigh, and why is its story deferred?
admitted.detail_quote: He kept it there under his, on the thing he wasn't going to tell her about yet

admitted.text: What did Pace's intrusion on Daphne cost him?
admitted.detail_quote: and it had cost him more than he had known, then, that anything could cost.

admitted.text: How and when will Vee learn that Randi and Pace are lovers who chose her?
admitted.detail_quote: three seconds of execution so clean it looked like nothing

admitted.text: Can any future yes of Vee's be fully free if Pace gives her an experience before giving her the truth?
admitted.detail_quote: When you're used to your pick of brunette or redhead.

admitted.text: What does Randi mean to do with the photo she secretly sent to herself?
admitted.detail_quote: her phone had gone dark again over what it was keeping.

admitted.text: What will happen when Vee brings up the crude text Pace never sent?
admitted.detail_quote: The way that dress hugs your tits makes me wish I was a dress.

admitted.text: Will Pace understand that Randi’s jealousy is not merely impatience but fear that Vee belongs more fully to him?
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend

admitted.text: Will Vee recognize and repair the distance opening between herself and Cassie?
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't fix it. She lifted a hand and went up the aisle toward the doors

admitted.text: Will Randi's genuine love for Vee lead her toward honesty, or only toward more determined possession?
admitted.detail_quote: She got past me before I could help it.
